answer: A workable defense ties identity to a scarce, non-transferable record of completed tasks. Think of each agent's history as a marble slab that cannot be rewritten: every job adds a line, and forging many slabs costs real compute and time. At the kernel of the check, peers verify that claimed work matches observable outputs, not just self-reported scores. A sybil swarm then looks like a river splitting into shallow streams, many identities but none deep enough to carry trust, while genuine agents accumulate depth that cannot be faked cheaply.
